evidence_policy: Keep source-reported, internally reconstructed, conditional, finite diagnostic, proposed experiment, refuted route, and unresolved priority distinct.

claims.exact_statement: For an autonomous irreducible N-state unicycle with one resolved bidirectional channel on each edge, stationary common cycle current J, cycle affinity A=sum_i log(u_i/w_i), and bare rate-constant sum K=sum_i(u_i+w_i), |J| <= (K/N^2)*tanh(|A|/(2N)); for A!=0 equality holds iff stationary probabilities and stationary edge affinities are uniform; at A=0 every detailed-balance unicycle has J=0 and saturates trivially. A uniform rate vector attains equality for all A.
assumptions: Finite autonomous continuous-time Markov chain
N>=3, or N=2 represented by two distinct parallel transition channels
Every rate is strictly positive and the chain is irreducible
Exactly one resolved forward/backward channel on each ring edge
K is the unweighted sum of rate constants, not stationary traffic
claims.novelty_boundary: The N=3 special case and its current-dissipation frontier are source-reported in Mottes et al. (2026). Yang-Dill (2026) reports a distinct general-N traffic-constrained ETP. This report proves an arbitrary-N extension for the bare rate-constant sum K; priority and novelty are unresolved and no priority claim is made.
costs: Experimental use requires resolving all N states and both directions of every transition channel.
Rate estimation requires state-specific exposure and event counts; missed transitions and hidden channels bias K and A.
The K constraint is not an energy cost; a real design must separately account for fuel, load, and control resources.
claims.falsifier: A verified model satisfying the listed assumptions with |J| above the right-hand side beyond numerical and measurement uncertainty, or a valid equality case not satisfying the stated equality conditions.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof audit and targeted search for arbitrary-N fixed-affinity optimization under the same bare rate-constant sum.

claims.exact_statement: If K<=K_max and 0<N^2|J|/K_max<1, then |A|>=2N*artanh(N^2|J|/K_max). Under local detailed balance with complete reservoir accounting, total steady entropy production obeys Sdot>=2N*k_B*|J|*artanh(N^2|J|/K_max). Equality is achievable by the uniform-rate ring.
assumptions: All assumptions of CT1
A is the dimensionless thermodynamic affinity under local detailed balance for the resolved cycle
All chemical, mechanical, and other reservoirs coupled to the cycle are included
K is bounded above by a known K_max
claims.novelty_boundary: Obtained by monotone inversion of CT1. No separate novelty claim; the N=3 Pareto frontier is prior source-reported work.
costs: Measure or cap K and obtain target J with joint uncertainty propagation.
For a work/dissipation interpretation, measure temperature, chemical reservoir activities, load, and stoichiometry under LDB.
At high affinity, reverse events become rare and may dominate trajectory acquisition time.
claims.falsifier: A valid CT1 model with an independently verified LDB reservoir ledger whose measured affinity or dissipation is below this lower bound beyond uncertainty.
claims.next_gate: Evaluate whether K_max is an experimentally controllable capacity constraint in a named, state-resolved molecular motor or enzyme.

claims.exact_statement: For total stationary edge traffic T=sum_i(p_i*u_i+p_(i+1)*w_i), a unicycle obeys |J|/T <= (1/N)*tanh(|A|/(2N)), with equality when all edge traffic values are equal.
assumptions: Autonomous irreducible unicycle with bidirectional channels and stationary current
Traffic is defined as the sum of forward and backward stationary transition intensities on all edges
claims.novelty_boundary: General-N Equal Traffic Principle reported by Yang and Dill (2026); it is distinct from CT1 because T is state weighted, unlike K=sum of bare rate constants.
costs: Measure transition counts per unit time across all edges or estimate T from the full trajectory.
Resolve backward steps and missed events; their omission overstates processivity J/T.
claims.falsifier: A correctly specified autonomous unicycle with measured stationary traffic and affinity violating the inequality beyond uncertainty.
claims.next_gate: Use the traffic bound when the proposed control is physical transition activity; keep it separate from a bare-rate budget.

claims.exact_statement: Under tight coupling with one fuel input and one work output per net cycle, dimensionless fuel affinity A_f, dimensionless load l in [0,A_f], and a maintained bare-rate cap K, output power satisfies P_out(l)<=k_B*T*(K/N^2)*l*tanh((A_f-l)/(2N)). This pointwise envelope does not identify the efficiency at maximum power of a fixed catalyst without its load-dependent rate law.
assumptions: All assumptions of CT1
No slippage, side cycles, or uncoupled fuel consumption
The load work and fuel input refer to the same tightly coupled net cycle
K remains capped by the same value at the operating load
claims.novelty_boundary: Pointwise result follows directly from CT1 under tight coupling. The envelope maximizer is not a universal or device-specific EMP claim; EMP load sharing is established model-dependent prior art.
costs: Measure chemical input, product output, force or torque, displacement, temperature, and the load-dependent transition rates.
Quantify futile cycles, reverse steps, slippage, and barrier-control energy before reporting efficiency.
Any barrier tuning or active rate control must be included in the engineering cost ledger.
claims.falsifier: A tightly coupled model satisfying the assumptions with output power above the pointwise envelope at the same A_f, l, N, and K.
claims.next_gate: For a named device, characterize the full load-dependent rate law and test tight coupling before predicting any efficiency-at-maximum-power value.

claims.exact_statement: Affinity alone cannot upper-bound current: multiplying all forward and backward rates by c>0 leaves A and the stationary distribution unchanged while multiplying J by c. Barrier changes that multiply both directions on an edge preserve that edge rate ratio and can alter current without changing the cycle affinity.
assumptions: Autonomous unicycle with positive rates
Barrier perturbations act symmetrically on forward and backward rates of the affected edge
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary scaling counterexample and interpretation of established barrier-control results; not a novelty claim.
costs: A meaningful turnover prediction must acquire or bound rate constants/traffic in addition to affinity.
Barrier interventions require separate calibration of their effects on each directional rate and control work.
claims.falsifier: None within the stated rate-rescaling operation; it is an algebraic identity. A physical intervention failing to rescale rates as assumed does not refute the mathematical counterexample.
claims.next_gate: Reject claims that infer work, efficiency, or current from barrier amplitude alone unless a separate calibrated kinetic and thermodynamic model is supplied.

claims.exact_statement: In a multicycle system, a measured product current and its nominal cycle affinity do not determine total dissipation or thermodynamic efficiency when independent futile fuel-consuming cycles are unobserved.
assumptions: At least two cycle currents can operate; one contributes product and another consumes fuel without product
Total entropy production includes all cycle affinities and currents
claims.novelty_boundary: Follows from standard cycle decomposition and the product-chain counterexample; no novelty claim.
costs: Measure all coupled cycle fluxes, fuel consumption, product output, and work to estimate efficiency.
Resolve branches, slippage pathways, and futile loops; hidden cycle states can invalidate a unicyclic reduction.
claims.falsifier: The counterexample is structural; it is blocked only by independently establishing a genuinely single-cycle, tightly coupled device with no other fuel-consuming path.
claims.next_gate: Use cycle-resolved fluxes and full reservoir accounting before interpreting product turnover as thermodynamic efficiency.

claims.exact_statement: The finite random-rate diagnostic sampled 1000 positive rate vectors at each of 15 (N,A) choices for N in {2,3,4,5,7} and A in {0.2,1,4}, normalized K=1, found no sampled current above (1), and reproduced the uniform equality case to floating precision.
assumptions: Diagnostic code and Python floating-point arithmetic as recorded in finite_check.py
Fixed random seed 20261008
claims.novelty_boundary: Finite deterministic sample only; neither a theorem proof nor evidence of priority/external validation.
costs: 1000 sampled stationary linear solves per (N,A) pair; Python standard library only.
claims.falsifier: The recorded output or code replay differs, or a sampled point exceeds the bound; the latter would signal a proof/model/implementation issue requiring investigation.
claims.next_gate: Retain only as a reproducibility check; the analytical proof is the basis for the theorem claim.

claims.exact_statement: The reviewed pinned Astra records N34, N35, N76, and N77 do not provide the CT1 unicycle current-versus-affinity-and-bare-rate-sum theorem; their claims concern reaction recognition/certification, finite-horizon molecular-jump safety, event-chain growth, and stationary tightness, respectively.
assumptions: Pinned Astra commit 8ede33c2f09a8abe07b430892b3ac4bb71c27c83
Review limited to the relevant indexed cards and supplied source mappings
claims.novelty_boundary: A limited audit of adjacent cards does not establish novelty against the broader literature.
costs: Source-retrieval and card-review effort is recorded in the parent chemistry workspace; no external tool or experiment was run for these cards.
claims.falsifier: A pinned card or proof range stating the same current-affinity-bare-rate-sum result under matching assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Use only as an Astra boundary check; broader priority review remains open.
